steps.text: Whisk oil, vinegar, sugar, parsley, basil, oregano, and salt together in a small bowl or measuring cup until vinaigrette is well combined.
Place cherry tomatoes in a serving dish; pour vinaigrette over tomatoes and gently stir to coat. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Gently stir salad from the bottom to the top, coating all tomatoes, before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Marinated Cherry Tomato Salad
raw_recipe.description: This marinated cherry tomato salad recipe features an herb-infused apple cider vinegar and oil vinaigrette that infuses flavor as it sits in the fridge.
raw_recipe.name: Marinated Cherry Tomato Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk oil, vinegar, sugar, parsley, basil, oregano, and salt together in a small bowl or measuring cup until vinaigrette is well combined.

Gently stir salad from the bottom to the top, coating all tomatoes, before serving.

review.reviewBody: I made this recipe for a potluck at work, and it was a hit. A few things I tweeked with this recipe: I made the vinaigrette the night before, using a hand blender to really get things combined. I used a combination of white wine vinegar and balsamic vinegar. I used Splenda instead of sugar (1-2 packets). I also added 1 t. of grated parmesan cheese to the vinaigrette. The next day I roasted 3 oz. of pine nuts. I combined the tomatoes and vinaigrette about 2 hours before serving, letting it sit out at room temperature. Just before serving, I added the roasted pine nuts and some shredded parmesan cheese. It looked really pretty in a white casserole dish. I’m making it again tonight, for my family and guests. It’s a great way to enjoy (and use up!) those cherry tomatoes fresh from the garden.

followed directions from Anne Cassens

(She made this recipe for a potluck at work.) A few things she changed with the recipe... She made the vinaigrette the night before, using a hand blender to really get things combined. Then used a combination of white wine vinegar & balsamic vinegar. Used Splenda instead of sugar (1-2 packets). Also added 1 tsp. of grated Parmesan cheese to the vinaigrette. The next day she roasted 3 oz. of pine nuts. Combined the tomatoes & vinaigrette @2 hours before serving, letting it sit out at room temperature. Just before serving, she added the roasted pine nuts & some shredded Parmesan cheese. It looked really "pretty" in a white casserole dish.

I made a few changes.... #1- I roasted on a grill the tomatoes in aluminum foil with the mentioned herbs for 15 to 18 minutes. #2- Substituted the vegetable oil for olive oil. The taste was very pleasurable and intense and my guest where surprised. I had some Romano cheese in a bowl if anyone wanted to add to the tomatoes. I also included some garlic bread which was an extra add-on as a side dish. Very spicy and delicious.......

This salad was fresh, light, and surprisingly good tasting using only a few ingredients. I followed the recipe as written. With the leftovers, I threw them on mixed greens and added some feta for a light lunch the next day (no need for any salad dressing as the marinade makes for a great dressing). I can't wait to try it with fresh herbs from my garden this summer. A good rule of thumb when using fresh herbs is to use 3 times the amount of dried herbs than called for.

I used olive oil (instead of vegetable oil, and balsamic vinegar (in place of cider vinegar). I like to poke my fork tines in the tomatoes first to make sure the marinade gets inside. Marinated 4 hours in tight cover plastic bowl. Everytime I opened the fridge, I flipped to coat the other side. Adding feta before serving is the finishing touch. I also serve this for company (something different instead of salad). Yummy!

I made this but used fresh herbs since they are in my garden right now: 3 tablespoons chopped parsley and 1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil. I don't grow oregano so I used the teaspoon listed in the recipe.

Made this and served with scallops and angel hair pasta. Flavors get happier with time....day 2 was even better. Used organIc cherry tomatoes, cider vinegar and EVOO. Did not put in fridge.....tomatoes are best left out.

I made this with multicolor grape tomatoes, fresh basil and oregano, balsamic vinegar, and a little grated parmesan. It was delicious and so visually appealing! I probably wouldn't make with all dried herbs, fresh is so flavorful. I did use dried parsley though.

What a great salad have on a hot day! The only changes I made: I used a tablespoon each of all fresh herbs because I had them growing. I love the salad, I had a hard time waiting two hours for the flavors to meld because it was so delicious!!?

Really delicious..

I followed some suggestions by others here. I subbed balsamic vinegar and left out the sugar. I added a clove of garlic.

Will definitely make again.

I just use equal amounts of apple cider vinegar, sugar, and vegetable oil and it's delicious! Adding in fresh ribbons of sweet basil, garlic salt and ground pepper gives it an extra boost. Crumbled feta cheese is the cherry on top!
This was easy to make. It was delicious when we had dinner that night and better the next day!
6.16.17 Fresh herbs, olive oil, and white balsamic vinegar are good choices for this refreshing salad that goes well with just about anything. Looks good, tastes good, and that’s good enough for me!

I have made this recipe--with halved or quartered grape tomatoes--several times for family and friends, and it is a total winner, literally to the last drop! Have also added mozzarella balls to it for a caprese-like salad...yummy. I am going to try adding cucumber chunks with the mozzarella balls, and serving it with toothpicks for an app. Thanks for the recipe.
I never thought of adding sugar to any dressing. I LOVE IT!
I’ve been eating tomatoes like this for 59 years. I can’t grow enough tomatoes 🍅. I add a pinch of sugar to take the bite out of the vinager
This would be great with little mozzarella balls also!
YUM!!!! Perfect summer side dish...can't keep my hands off it till dinner time!
